stem.en: Kabir says: "If a gene can be spliced five ways, that is really five genes." What is the difference?

text.en: Five genes would be five separate recipes, each copied from its own promoter and mutated separately. Five splicings of one gene share a promoter, a copy, and every letter of every exon; a mutation in a shared exon changes all five at once.

feedback.en: They come from one stretch of tape under one start sign. Count genes by promoters, not by proteins.

text.en: Five splicings is fewer than one gene.

feedback.en: A gene is a recipe region. This one gives five products, which is more, not fewer.

text.en: Alternative splicing means the gene is broken.

feedback.en: It is regulated, not broken. Different cells choose different splicings on purpose.

explanation.en: A gene is a stretch of tape with a promoter. What it yields can be one protein or several. The tape is one thing.
